editorial:
Imagine moving your whole family to a new city for a dream job, only to realize your marriage is falling apart. That is exactly what happens to Paulo, a PR guy who heads to Brasília to help a senator win another term. He brings along his wife, Cris, and their young daughter, but there is a huge problem. They are not actually in love. They only stayed together because of their child, who was a surprise pregnancy they weren't ready for. The movie feels heavy and honest, showing you how hard it is to fake a happy life when you are surrounded by political lies and personal sadness.

What really works here is the acting. You can feel the tension between the husband and wife in every single scene. It is not a fast movie, but it keeps you interested because you want to see if they will finally break up or find a way to fix things. If you enjoy stories about messy relationships and political secrets, you should definitely check this out. You can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or you might want to rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The story ends with the couple finally facing the truth about their broken marriage. After trying to keep up appearances for the senator and their daughter, they realize that staying together is doing more harm than good. There is no magical happy ending where they fall back in love. Instead, they accept that their relationship is over. They decide to separate but agree to be good parents to their daughter, choosing honesty over a fake life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic dramas about family struggles and politics.
